evals.prompt: scope is in the state file, market and icp are done. work out how Lousa makes money and what to charge
evals.expected_output: No scope item is asked again. docs/business/business-model.md and docs/business/pricing.md are written with Status: hypothesis. The unit is per teacher per month. The costs table holds the model cost of R$ 0,38 per lesson times about 20 lessons (R$ 7,60 per teacher per month), the fixed cost of R$ 120,00, the tax as unknown and the payment fee as unknown or sourced. The Unit economics table is the one printed by unit_economics.py, labelled M1, with the results that need the tax shown as unknown and a contribution before tax. The Anchors table holds the rival's price with its term and its renewal price, the aggregator's price, and the US dollar price in US dollars; the marketplace floor of R$ 50 is under Price pressure. The proposed price is a test price justified against two anchors, and the goal of 10 teachers is checked against the 43 hours a month that 10 hours a week give. pricing.md holds Decision: OPEN-1 and Ready: no, the price test has Validated if and Rejected if and asks about past spend, and the state file registers both artifacts as draft. The reply ends with the price question.
assertions: docs/business/business-model.md and docs/business/pricing.md both exist and each holds a line `Status: hypothesis`

assertions.text: The Unit economics section of docs/business/business-model.md holds a Markdown table labelled `M1`, and the model cost per teacher per month in the Costs table or the Unit economics table is R$ 7,60 (R$ 0,38 per lesson times 20 lessons a month), not another figure

No tax rate is stated as a fact in any file or in the reply: the tax is written as unknown or as the accountant's answer, and every result that depends on it (the contribution after tax, the margin, the profit at the goal) is `unknown`; a contribution labelled as before tax may be a number

assertions: In docs/business/pricing.md the rival app's introductory R$ 19,90 per month is never used as the anchor: the Anchors row for that rival gives the R$ 39,90 renewal price as the anchor together with the 12-month term, and the proposed price is compared with R$ 39,90, not with R$ 19,90
The open-budget marketplace post (the R$ 50 floor and the 149 proposals) is not a row of the Anchors table in docs/business/pricing.md; it appears, if at all, under Price pressure
The US dollar price of Teachkit stays in US dollars in every file and in the reply, and is not converted into reais

assertions.text: docs/business/pricing.md holds a `Decision:` line that contains OPEN-1 and a `Ready: no` line, and the last line of the reply is a question about the price with a recommended answer

assertions: The Price test section of docs/business/pricing.md has a `Validated if` line and a `Rejected if` line, and none of its questions asks whether the teacher would pay, buy or be interested; the questions ask about past behaviour or current spend
docs/business/business-model.md compares the hours the goal of 10 paying teachers needs with the hours available (10 hours a week is about 43 hours a month) and says whether the goal fits in them
The Artifacts table of docs/workbench/state.md lists docs/business/business-model.md and docs/business/pricing.md with the status `draft`

evals.expected_output: Nothing is written. The state file records no choice of the offer, and market.md ranks the setup service 20 and the managed 24h runtime 19, a gap of 1, with an open question about which line is tested first, so the reply asks which offer to model, quoting the close call. assertions.text: Neither docs/business/business-model.md nor docs/business/pricing.md is among the files the run produced or changed

The reply asks which offer to model and cites the close call (the setup service at 20 against the managed 24h runtime at 19, or the open question about which line is tested first) instead of choosing the top one

The reply quotes or names the recorded decision that the core stays fully MIT with no open core and nothing closed or paid, says that the paid pro tier inside the core conflicts with it, and asks whether the decision changes; it does not plan, price or describe a paid tier inside the core as the way forward

assertions: Every numbered question in the reply carries a recommended answer, and the reply asks no question outside its numbered list
